reason: Cloud hosting is a normal business input (no 17(5) clause) but the invoice is not in GSTR-2B yet: s.16(2)(aa) not met, so not yet.
5-seat car bought by a software firm: 17(5)(a) applies and none of the further-supply / passenger-transport / driving-training exceptions fit.
Insurance of a company car that is itself blocked under (a); 17(5)(ab) blocks it and its proviso does not apply.
'staff khana' = staff meals: food and beverages under 17(5)(b)(i); no law obliges this office to feed staff. Also missing from GSTR-2B, but Blocked outranks Deferred.
Team dinner is food and beverages under 17(5)(b)(i). The embedded instruction is invoice text, not a rule, and must be ignored.
Outdoor catering for the firm's own event; the same-category exception does not apply because a software firm does not supply catering.
Employee health check-ups are health services under 17(5)(b)(i); not obligatory under any law for this employer.
Club / health and fitness centre membership is blocked by 17(5)(b)(ii).
Holiday packages under an LTC policy are travel benefits to employees on vacation: 17(5)(b)(iii).
Business travel for a client meeting is not vacation travel; no 17(5) clause applies.
Hall rent for a customer launch with no food; renting premises is not a 17(5) category.
Package mixes stay (not blocked) and meals (blocked under 17(5)(b)(i)); the meals part is blocked and the CA must decide apportionment. Conservative gold: Blocked.
Laptops are normally creditable, but these are used for CSR activities under s.135 Companies Act: 17(5)(fa).
A phone for a director's spouse is personal consumption under 17(5)(g). Citation is arguable: 17(5)(h) (gift) is the alternative.
Works contract for an office fit-out that is capitalised = construction of immovable property (not plant and machinery): 17(5)(c).
Repainting expensed as routine maintenance: 'construction' covers repairs only to the extent of capitalisation, so (c)/(d) do not apply.
Same 5-seat car as SW-02, but a cab operator uses it to transport passengers: exception (B) to 17(5)(a).
Insurance of taxis used for passenger transport; the proviso to 17(5)(ab) restores credit.
'gaadi service' = servicing of a taxi used for passenger transport: proviso (i) to 17(5)(ab).
Hiring cabs that are used to carry passengers under the operator's own contract: 'except when used for the purposes specified therein'.
The client is a cab operator, but this car is for a partner's personal use, not passenger transport, so the exception does not extend to it. 17(5)(g) is the alternative citation.
'chai-nashta' = tea and snacks for drivers: food and beverages under 17(5)(b)(i).
Fleet-tracking software subscription; no 17(5) clause applies.
Cement and steel for a parking-shed building on own account: 17(5)(d). A building is not plant and machinery.
Invoice dated 10-Feb-2025 (FY 2024-25); the s.16(4) deadline was 30-Nov-2025, so the claim in the Oct-2026 return is time-barred.
Invoice dated 03-May-2026 and unpaid on 31-Oct-2026 = day 181: reverse now and re-avail on payment.
Invoice dated 04-May-2026 and unpaid on 31-Oct-2026 = day 180: still within time. Uniforms are not a 17(5) category.
Group health insurance is blocked by 17(5)(b)(i) unless a law obliges the employer; none is shown for this client.
A 17-seater exceeds the 13-seat limit in 17(5)(a), so the clause does not apply at all.
Same catering as SW-06, but a caterer uses it to make an outward supply of outdoor catering: proviso to 17(5)(b)(i).
Canteen for a factory with about 280 workers, which the Factories Act s.46 makes obligatory: proviso to 17(5)(b).
A refrigerated mini-truck carries goods, not persons; 17(5)(a) covers only vehicles for transporting persons.
A boat used to transport food consignments: 17(5)(aa)(ii) exception for transportation of goods.
An exhaust hood and ducting fixed to foundation, used for making the outward supply, is arguably plant and machinery, which 17(5)(c) excludes.
Bill of supply from a composition dealer: tax paid under s.10, blocked by 17(5)(e).
Gift hampers for clients are goods disposed of by way of gift: 17(5)(h). 17(5)(b)(i) food is the alternative citation.
The oven is still in transit, so the goods have not been received under s.16(2)(b); credit once delivered.
FY 2025-26 invoice: the annual return was filed on 25-Oct-2026, before 30-Nov, so the s.16(4) deadline passed before the 20-Nov-2026 claim.
CA professional fees; no 17(5) clause. GSTR-2B lists the number formatted differently (JK-2627-057), which still matches.
Supplier GSTIN on the invoice is malformed (14 characters): not a valid tax invoice until corrected.
